summary: Consolidated the valid MPS working-set accounting from candidate PR https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/pull/2901 and corrected the counterexamples independently reported by review PR https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/pull/2972. MPS total and available memory remain capped by torch.mps.recommended_max_memory() on the supported path. Missing, raising, invalid, or non-positive safety inputs now fail closed instead of falling back to uncapped host RAM. Available-memory accounting also fails closed when driver allocation usage cannot be determined. The registered unit test now uses only the CPU CI registry required by repository taxonomy.

tests.what_was_measured: The candidate's original focused suite passed 10 tests, establishing that the review counterexamples were absent from its regression coverage. Raw output: /job/reports-j-5c1b25490e43-raw/candidate-focused-tests.txt

tests.what_was_measured: All five candidate cases returned host values of 64 GiB total and 60 GiB available, reproducing the unsafe fallback before correction. Raw output: /job/reports-j-5c1b25490e43-raw/candidate-counterexamples.txt
Repository taxonomy rejected the unit test's MLX registration: unit tests may register only CPU suites. Raw output: /job/reports-j-5c1b25490e43-raw/candidate-taxonomy.txt
23 corrected compatibility, adversarial, pressure, over-allocation, and production-integration tests passed. Raw output: /job/reports-j-5c1b25490e43-raw/corrected-focused-tests.txt

All applicable repository hooks passed, including registered-test taxonomy. Raw output: /job/reports-j-5c1b25490e43-raw/corrected-precommit.txt
Every changed Python source and test file compiled successfully. Raw output: /job/reports-j-5c1b25490e43-raw/compileall.txt

gpu_execution_evidence: The prepared host is Linux/x86_64 with Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2; torch.backends.mps.is_built() and is_available() are both false. AMD GPU execution cannot validate Apple Metal memory accounting. Environment output: /job/reports-j-5c1b25490e43-raw/environment.txt
remaining_limitations: No Apple Silicon/MPS device was available, so the native torch.mps values were not compared with MTLDevice.recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize.
No MPS model-loading, KV-cache, UMA pressure, paging, or stability workload was run; deterministic mocks exercised the actual Python production call paths.

Runtimes without working recommended_max_memory and driver_allocated_memory APIs are intentionally unsupported for automatic MPS memory sizing because no verified safe device-specific fallback is available.
No native rebuild was applicable because the correction is Python-only.
